public_rationale: Sora became available to Plus and Pro subscribers on December 9, 2024. A January 14, 2025 research report subsequently documented recurring object hallucinations and continuity-related errors in Sora. That meets the early-resolution rule for further recurring glitches following expanded access. No deadline needs to be supplied.
limitations: The evaluation concerns later publicly accessible Sora, not a controlled retest of the February preview.
Benchmark scores combine several kinds of error and do not establish their architectural cause.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: As more people gain access to Sora, more systemic glitches will be found.

statement.excerpt: We will, I am certain, see more systemic glitches as more people have access.

from_speaker: We will, I am certain, see more systemic glitches
our_interpretation: Expanded access means access beyond the original restricted preview group.
More glitches means further documented instances of recurring physics or continuity problems; they need not be entirely new failure categories.
The forecast concerns the continuing Sora product, including subsequent releases.
criteria.support_condition: After expanded access, credible testing documents additional recurring physics, object or continuity errors in Sora.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A finite period without reports cannot contradict this undated forecast. Conclusive contradiction would require a terminal event eliminating further access and a sufficiently complete record showing no additional recurring failures.

evidence.explanation: The preceding sentence identifies object hallucinations, unwanted camera movement and shot changes; the researchers report these recurring in Sora evaluations. The date marks public documentation of the findings, not a claimed exact generation date.
